correctness.rationale: A finite generalized hexagon order(q,q) has intersection array {q+1,q,q,q,q,q;1,1,1,1,1,q+1} and six distance matrices A_j=P_j(A). Independently derived P0..P6 by three-term recurrence with final divisor q+1. Sympy factored terminal identity tP6−qP5=−t(q−t²)(3q−t²)(q−t+1)(q+t+1)/(q+1), yielding adjacency spectrum +/- (q+1), 0, +/-sqrt(q), +/-sqrt(3q). At t=−(q+1) computed signed shell eigenvalues: 1, −(q+1), (q+1)q, −(q+1)q², (q+1)q³, −(q+1)q^4, q^5. They give exact F_q(p) as claimed. Its derivative at p=0 is q^5 log(6/5)−q^4 log(5/4)+...>0.179q^5 for q>=100; |F_q double prime|<7q^5 on [0,10q^-5] and F_q(10q^-5)>0 ensure unique crossing. All other five nonconstant eigenvalues remain <−0.96 under the source bounds |Lambda+1|<4000 q^-5/2<0.04, hence sole critical one-dimensional point-line contrast. Schoenberg monotonicity excludes reentrance. Taylor gives alpha_q=1/(q^5 log(6/5))+log(5/4)/(q^6 log²(6/5))+O(q^-7), and Gram ranks |X|−1 below and |X|−2 at root. Numeric/finite spectral checks are subordinate to these uniform bounds.

value.rationale: The first exponent at which a canonical generalized-polygon incidence metric ceases to embed in Hilbert space after snowflaking is a natural exact invariant. A sharp q^-5 law, two-term asymptotic and unique bipartition critical direction for every existing high-order generalized hexagon reveal a structural growth phenomenon not mechanically implied by general Schoenberg theory.

limitations: Every finite generalized hexagon of order(q,q) with q>=100 if it exists; no unequal order, smaller q, generalized octagon or all infinite metrics.
